mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate below 1.5% consistently indicates accommodative monetary policy that lowers discount rates for equity valuation, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days without regime dependency.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in >55% of periods when FEDFUNDS < 1.5%, or Rank IC < 0.02 over any 5-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate decline exceeding 0.2 percentage points signals labor market tightening that boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are negative in >55% of instances with UNRATE monthly change < -0.2, or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous retail sales (RSAFS) and housing starts (HOUST) above their 12-month moving averages indicate broad-based consumer and housing demand expansion, triggering positive S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days through improved revenue visibility.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in >55% of instances with both RSAFS and HOUST above 12mo MA, or interaction effect p-value > 0.05 in regression model.

mechanism_narrative: Declining industrial production below 100 (INDPRO) signals manufacturing contraction and rising recession risk, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in >55% of periods when INDPRO < 100, or Rank IC < 0.02 over 5-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Real GDP growth above its 4-quarter moving average (GDPC1) indicates sustained economic expansion that supports corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days without conditional triggers.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in >55% of periods when GDPC1 > 4q MA, or Rank IC < 0.02 over 5-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Accelerating inflation (CPIAUCSL monthly change > 2.5%) prompts Federal Reserve monetary tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 5 trading days due to rising real interest rates.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in >55% of instances with CPIAUCSL monthly change > 2.5%, or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent unemployment rate decline (UNRATE monthly change < 0) and payroll growth exceeding 100,000 (PAYEMS > 100) indicate a strong labor market that enhances consumer confidence and drives positive S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in >55% of instances with UNRATE monthly change < 0 and PAYEMS > 100, or interaction term p-value > 0.05 in regression model.

mechanism_narrative: In low-inflation regimes (CPIAUCSL YoY change < 2.0%), a federal funds rate increase above 1.0% signals monetary tightening that reduces equity attractiveness, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in >55% of periods with CPIAUCSL YoY change < 2.0% and FEDFUNDS > 1.0%, or Rank IC < 0.02 over 5-year rolling window.
